text:
Next Tuesday I'm heading to Midtown for Corvanta's session, "Operationalizing AI-native revenue intelligence at enterprise scale."

The title is a mouthful, but the substance is something every GTM team deals with: knowing which deals will slip before the quarter ends.

Corvanta's product reads call recordings and CRM history to flag deals likely to slip in the current quarter. One of their customers, a 200-rep software company, says it cut its end-of-quarter forecast miss from 18% to 7%. I want to hear how that happened in practice.

Tomasz Arkwright-Bell, Corvanta's head of sales operations, is speaking. I'm hoping he gets into the unglamorous parts:

→ What changed in how reps and managers run pipeline reviews
→ How much the flags depend on clean CRM data
→ What happens when the model and a rep's gut disagree

Forecast accuracy is one of those problems where a few points of improvement change how a whole company plans hiring, spend, and board conversations. I'm curious whether the results hold up outside a single customer story.

If you're going, say hi. I'd like to compare notes afterward on what's real and what's still slideware.
